cycle.rule: Next topic is the first topic strictly after cycle.last in the enumerated syllabus order whose status is not covered, wrapping at the end. not_started and partial topics are candidates; blocked topics are skipped while their blocker stands.

topics.name: Propositional Logic
topics.coverage_note: Built in run 2 from one playlist only (GO Classes for GATE CS, Propositional Logic). Four videos had Devanagari ASR captions only and were not used for any formula. Nineteen of the topic's PYQs are SOURCED rather than key-verified.
gaps: four videos readable only as Hindi ASR fragments; two GATE questions they cover (2006, 2015 Q.28) are not in the PYQ set
no re-audit of the syllabus subtopics since the topic was built from a single playlist

topics.name: First Order Logic
topics.coverage_note: Built in run 3 from one playlist only (GO Classes for GATE CS, First Order Logic). One video returned no caption text at all; the rest were readable only in their opening minutes.
gaps: video zdeKQ-nABtk returned no caption text on any route, so nothing is claimed about what it teaches
resolution and prenex normal form in first order logic are not taught by any processed source

topics.name: Sets, Relations, Functions
topics.coverage_note: 11 cards, one per subtopic (sets and cardinality, power sets, set identities, Cartesian product, countability, relation representation and counting, relation properties, transitivity and closure, equivalence relations and partitions, function counting, composition and inverse), 7 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because three gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit: one IIT/NPTEL-style lecture for set identities, Cartesian product and relation properties (full transcript); two TrevTutor lectures for set basics and for injective/surjective/bijective functions (full transcripts); the GO Classes Set Theory playlist for GATE question patterns (opening readable only).

gaps: no verified GATE CSE previous-year question exists in this topic for countability of infinite sets; GATE tests countability inside Theory of Computation questions (for example GATE CSE 2019 Q.34 on recursively enumerable languages), so that question is left for the Theory of Computation run
relation closures (reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure and Warshall) are taught from Rosen ch. 9.4 only - no lecture transcript for closures was readable
the GO Classes Set Theory PYQ lecture used here (Relations - GATE PYQs Part 2) was readable only in its opening, so its later question types are not recorded

topics.name: Partial Orders and Lattices
topics.coverage_note: 11 subtopics, 12 cards (poset axioms, Hasse diagram and covering, chains/antichains and total orders, minimal/maximal/least/greatest, bounds and LUB/GLB, the lattice test, the lattice laws, sublattices, bounded and complemented lattices, distributive lattices, Boolean and divisor lattices, complete lattices), 6 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because three gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit across three channels: the IIT Madras Lecture 40 transcript (English, read in full) for the lattice laws, the M3 and pentagon counterexamples, complements and the antichain decomposition; NPTEL IIT Guwahati Lec 21-23 for the poset-to-lattice sequence and the divisor example (captions unavailable); GO Classes for the GATE question patterns (1993, 1996, 2003 readable as an auto-caption excerpt; 2017, 2024, 1997 video captions unavailable). A 16-video Hindi playlist by Sandeep Kumar Gour, the NPTEL IIT Roorkee 2015 chapters and the Neso Academy sequence were considered and rejected, with reasons in sources.json. No card is translated: no readable source was non-English.

gaps: video captions could not be retrieved in this run (YouTube caption endpoints answered LOGIN_REQUIRED and the third-party transcript service was blocked), so four chosen video sources are recorded as structure-only and no card quotes or timestamps them; Lecture 40 exists as a published transcript PDF and was read in full

three Hasse-diagram PYQs are figure-only in the papers and could not be recomputed from text, so they are not in the PYQ set: GATE CSE 1997 Q.3.3 (complements of an element, quoted from GATE Overflow as three), GATE CSE 2005 Q.9 (lattice but not distributive) and GATE CSE 2015 Set 1 Q.34 (probability that the distributive law holds in a five-element lattice)

Birkhoff's forbidden-sublattice characterisation (distributive iff no M3 or N5 sublattice) is stated from the standard reference only - it is not recomputed by enumeration in scripts/validate.py, which checks only the one direction on the two counterexamples

topics.name: Monoids and Groups
topics.coverage_note: 11 subtopics, 11 cards (the algebraic-structure ladder, monoids and the identity, group axioms and the reversal rule, order of a group and of an element, abelian groups and the two commutativity tests, subgroups and the one-step test, cyclic groups and generators, cosets and Lagrange's theorem, the small cast of groups GATE reuses, group homomorphisms and the kernel, permutation groups), 13 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because four gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit across two languages: the GeeksforGeeks GATE group-theory notes (English) for the ladder, the group properties, the subgroup tests and Lagrange's theorem, because it was the only GATE-oriented written source whose full text could be read this run; the Pradeep Giri 'Algebraic Structure' lecture (Hindi auto-captions, read in part) for the rung-by-rung construction, the only non-English source used and the only translated material in the topic; the GO Classes Module 7 lecture list (structure only) to confirm the subtopic enumeration is complete. The NPTEL IIT Madras 'Algebras' lectures 35-37, the NPTEL Introduction to Abstract Group Theory, the Knowledge Gate Hindi playlist, the Dr. Gajendra Purohit playlist and several GATE answer aggregators were considered and rejected, with reasons in sources.json.

gaps: video captions could not be retrieved in this run (YouTube watch pages carried no caption tracks and the timedtext endpoint returned an empty body), so the GO Classes lecture sequence is recorded as structure-only and no card quotes or timestamps a lecture

the NPTEL IIT Madras 'Algebras' transcripts (lectures 35-37) - the same course that supplied the full-text Lecture 40 used for the previous topic - could not be fetched, because the host refused the request from the sandbox; no claim rests on them and a later run should retry

quotient groups, normal subgroups, Cauchy's and Sylow's theorems and group actions are outside the GATE line and are not covered at all; the homomorphism card is the only material beyond the two words 'Monoids, Groups'

GATE CSE 1999 Q.4 (the three-part descriptive question that proves Lagrange from cosets) is excluded because the repository's PYQ schema holds only MCQ, MSQ and NAT records; the cosets card covers the same content
only one non-English source was readable (Hindi auto-captions) and its contribution is the structure ladder alone; no Tamil, Telugu or Bengali group-theory lecture could be read this run

topics.name: Graphs: Connectivity, Matching, Colouring
topics.coverage_note: 11 subtopics, 11 cards (graph vocabulary and the handshake lemma, paths/cycles/components and the n-k and C(n-k+1,2) bounds, cut vertices and bridges with both DFS rules, vertex and edge connectivity, Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, bipartite graphs and the odd-cycle criterion, matching maximal versus maximum with augmenting paths, Hall's marriage theorem, vertex cover/independent set/Koenig, chromatic number with greedy and Brooks bounds, chromatic polynomial), 9 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because five gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit: the GATE Overflow GO Classroom deck 'Graph Theory: Connectivity, Coloring, Matching' (English, read in part) because its title is the syllabus line and its pages were the only GATE-oriented graph text readable this run; the GATE Overflow subject notes (English, read in part) to confirm the subtopic enumeration against GATE's own question record; the NPTEL IIITB lectures 44-52 (English, structure only) to confirm the teaching order. Rejected with reasons in sources.json: the NPTEL 'Graph Theory' course by Soumen Maity (right scope, no readable transcript), GeeksforGeeks (host unreachable), Gate Vidyalay (snippet only), the Knowledge Gate AI colouring blog (a question dump), the answer aggregators (numbering disagreements) and every video in every language (YouTube consent wall, no caption tracks). No translated material appears: no non-English source was readable, so no card is marked as translated.

gaps: no video source was readable this run - YouTube served a consent wall with no caption tracks for every video tried, so no English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture supplied a single sentence and no card quotes or timestamps one

four PYQs of this topic are figure-only in the papers and are therefore not in the PYQ set: GATE CSE 2024 Set 2 Q.50 (chromatic number of a drawn graph), GATE CSE 2018 Q.18 (chromatic number of a drawn graph) and GATE CSE 1999 Q.1.15 (number of articulation points of a drawn graph); GATE CSE 2022 Q.40 is included but its isomorphism option rests on the paper's drawing, which is not re-derived here
planar graphs, Euler's formula for plane graphs, edge colouring and network flow beyond bipartite matching are outside the three words of this syllabus line and are not covered at all

GATE Overflow's subject page lists further graph-theory questions from 2010 to 2023 (for example 2012 Q.38, 2016 Set 2 Q.3, 2019 Q.38, 2020 Q.52, 2023 Q.45) that were not individually read or recomputed in this run; only the nine recorded PYQs were verified
the chromatic polynomial card rests on the standard references and on recomputation, because no verified GATE CSE previous-year question on the chromatic polynomial was found in this run
no marks field is recorded on any PYQ of this topic: the official papers were not fetched, so question numbers follow the GATE Overflow paper numbering and marks are left out rather than guessed

topics.coverage_note: Built in runs 1 and 2 from one playlist only (GO Classes for GATE CS, Combinatorics). The run reports record partial transcripts for the long lectures. The subtopic list has not been re-audited against the GATE 2027 line since.
gaps: no re-audit of the syllabus subtopics since the topic was built from a single playlist
long lecture transcripts were readable only in their opening minutes

topics.name: Matrices and Determinants
topics.coverage_note: 11 subtopics, 11 cards (matrix vocabulary and types, addition and scalar multiplication, the multiplication conformability rule and non-commutativity, transpose with symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices, powers with the idempotent/involutory/nilpotent/orthogonal identities, trace and the cyclic law, the determinant by minors and cofactors, the row and column operation laws, adjoint and inverse, rank with its bounds, and the singular-matrix equivalence list), 13 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because seven gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit across two languages: five full-text IIT Madras CS6015 slide decks (English, every page carrying a text layer) for the definitions, the multiplication and transpose rules, the elimination pivot count, the inverse and the determinant as a signed volume; the GATE Overflow linear algebra notes (English, read in part) for the GATE property and pitfall lists; the GeeksforGeeks GATE notes (English, read in part) for the adjoint, inverse, trace and rank property lists; one Hindi Class-12 one-shot (read only in its opening, translated, marked as translated) for the elementary vocabulary and operation laws; and the NPTEL IIT Roorkee Numerical Linear Algebra lecture list (structure only) to confirm the subtopic enumeration. The only non-English source used is Hindi.

gaps: no GATE-oriented lecture was readable: every English GATE linear-algebra video page tried carried no caption track, so the teaching rests on the IIT Madras slide decks and two GATE revision texts, and no card quotes or timestamps a GATE lecture

the adjoint and inverse card carries no verified PYQ: the only GATE CSE inverse question found in this topic, 1994 Q.3.12 ('Find the inverse of the matrix ...'), is descriptive, and the repository's PYQ schema holds only MCQ, MSQ and NAT records

no marks field is recorded on any PYQ of this topic: the official papers and keys were not fetched, so every question reference follows the numbering on the GATE Overflow question page and marks are left out rather than guessed

the one non-English source is a Class-12 Hindi one-shot read only in its opening, and it contributes only the elementary vocabulary, the matrix types and the operation laws; no GATE-level Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture could be read this run

three full-text GATE note sets that would have deepened the topic could not be fetched from the sandbox (Ankur Gupta's GATE engineering-mathematics PDF, the Vidyalankar GATE mathematics notes, and the NPTEL IIT Kanpur Linear Algebra book, whose host returned 404); nothing rests on them and a later run should retry

every PYQ in the topic is SOURCED against a GATE Overflow accepted answer rather than key-verified against an official answer key; only GATE CSE 2022 Q.10 has an independent corroboration of the official option, from the GateAI PYQ page and the GeeksforGeeks answer key
the GATE Overflow subject page lists further linear algebra questions from 2010 to 2019 that were not individually read or recomputed; only the thirteen recorded PYQs were verified

topics.name: System of Linear Equations
topics.coverage_note: 11 subtopics, 11 cards (matrix form with the row and column pictures, the consistency test by rank, the square determinant test, free variables and the shape of the solution set, homogeneous systems, Gaussian elimination with back substitution, parameter-dependent systems, overdetermined and underdetermined systems, the inverse and Cramer's rule, the geometry of the three cases, and telling no solution apart from infinitely many), 12 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because nine gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit across two languages: the GATE Overflow notes on Strang's first ten lectures (English, read in part) for the column picture and the particular-plus-null-space decomposition; SATHEE IIT Kanpur (English, read in part) for the rank criterion and the plane-arrangement table; the Vidyalankar GATE notes section 1.4 (English, read in part) for the consistency cases, Cramer's rule and the homogeneous condition; an Ohio University lecture (English, read in part) for the rank theorem and the rank(A) = m corollary; one Hindi chapter (translated, read in part) for the three-case table and the zero-determinant warning; and the GO Classes lecture list (structure only) to confirm the subtopic enumeration. No video transcript could be retrieved this run, so no card quotes or timestamps a lecture. Rejected with reasons in sources.json: the NPTEL IIT Roorkee Matrix Analysis lectures 4-5, the NPTEL IIT Kharagpur lectures 36-38, MIT OCW 18.06 Lecture 8, two Hindi Unacademy lessons, the Knowledge Gate Hindi live class (only an English AI summary is readable), a Testbook Hindi question bank drawn from other branches, and a GATE Overflow discussion thread that states one rule wrongly.

gaps: no video transcript could be retrieved this run: every YouTube watch page tried carried no caption track and the transcript service was refused by the egress proxy, so the GO Classes linear algebra lecture sequence (3B-3D, 5D-5E, 6A-6C) is recorded as structure-only and no card quotes or timestamps a lecture

the two best-scoped lecture series found, the NPTEL IIT Roorkee 'Matrix Analysis with Applications' lectures 4-5 and the NPTEL IIT Kharagpur 'Engineering Mathematics I' lectures 36-38, answered 404 on every transcript path tried from the sandbox; nothing rests on them and a later run should retry

two chosen English sources (Vidyalankar, Ohio University) were readable only through the search service extract because their PDFs returned 502 from the sandbox, so their contribution is limited to the sections quoted and neither was read in full

MIT OCW 18.06 Lecture 8, the canonical treatment of the complete solution, returned an empty body to the fetch service; its content reached the topic only indirectly through the GATE Overflow notes that summarise the same lectures
no marks field is recorded on any PYQ of this topic: only the GATE 2026 CS2 paper was fetched, and every other question reference follows the GATE Overflow numbering

every PYQ in the topic is SOURCED against a GATE Overflow accepted answer rather than key-verified; GATE CSE 2026 Set 2 Q.31 was located in the official paper at IIT Guwahati but the official answer key was not fetched, and GATE CSE 2014 Set 1 Q.52 rests on three secondary sources agreeing on 1
GATE CSE 2008 Q.3 is a defective question: a unique solution needs alpha other than 5, and no printed option states that, so the record says so instead of picking the nearest option
the only non-English source is a Hindi JEE-oriented chapter read in part; no GATE-level Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture on this topic could be read this run
GATE Overflow lists further linear-systems questions that were not individually read or recomputed, including GATE CSE 2004 Q.33 on finding x, y, z and GATE CSE 2001 Q.37 on sums of singular matrices

topics.name: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
topics.coverage_note: 12 subtopics, 11 cards (the definition with v nonzero, the characteristic equation and its degree-n roots, the eigenspace and computing eigenvectors, the trace and determinant identities with the eigenvalues of A^k, A^-1, A^T and p(A), algebraic against geometric multiplicity, diagonalisability, real symmetric matrices with orthogonal eigenvectors, complex conjugate pairs in a real matrix, the triangular / row-sum / all-ones / rank-one shortcuts, what preserves eigenvalues and the row-operation trap, and Cayley-Hamilton with the inverse from it), 10 verified PYQs and 1 p5.js lesson. Partial because six gaps remain, named below.

runs.note: Sources chosen on merit across two languages, with one lecture readable end to end. NPTEL IIT Kharagpur Lecture 46 (English, read in full) carries the definition, the characteristic equation, the eigenspace and Cayley-Hamilton, and is the only lecture this run whose transcript ran from the opening to the closing references. NPTEL-NOC IIT Madras CS7015 Lec 6.1 (English, read in part) supplies the geometric framing and the steady-state motivation. GanitAnk's Hindi one-shot (translated, read in part) is the only readable non-English source and gives the 3x3 principal-minor form of the characteristic polynomial and the Cayley-Hamilton inverse example. The GATE Overflow linear algebra notes (English, read in part) give the AM and GM definitions and the property list. The NPTEL course index is recorded as structure only. Rejected with reasons in sources.json: MIT OCW 18.06 Lecture 21 (page carried a summary and a transcript link, no transcript body), NPTEL IIT Kharagpur Lecture 49 (index only), the Unacademy Hindi eigen lesson series (paywalled, no transcript), the formula-list pages (properties without derivation, one of them stating the symmetric facts as general), the GO Classes DPP question bank (practice questions, not PYQs) and the answer aggregators (corroboration only, and they disagree on question numbering).

gaps: no GATE-oriented coaching lecture on this topic could be read: the readable lecture is a general engineering-mathematics NPTEL course, so the GATE-specific teaching order and PYQ walkthroughs are recorded as structure only

MIT OCW 18.06 Lecture 21, the canonical English treatment, returned a page with a one-sentence summary and a transcript link but no transcript body, so nothing could be read from it; a later run should retry

NPTEL IIT Kharagpur Lecture 49, the continuation that would have covered diagonalisation and symmetric matrices in the lecturer's voice, had no retrievable transcript, so the symmetric-matrix card rests on the standard references plus computation

the Hindi source was read in part only, and no GATE-level Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Bengali lecture with a readable transcript was found this run; the Unacademy Hindi series that matched the topic lesson-for-lesson is paywalled

every PYQ in this topic is SOURCED against a GATE Overflow accepted answer rather than key-verified against an official key, and no marks field is recorded: the official papers were not fetched this run, so references follow the GATE Overflow numbering and each record says where another site numbers the question differently

GATE Overflow lists further eigenvalue questions in this subject that were not individually read or recomputed, including the 2010 to 2013 entries, 2019 Q.44, 2022 Q.35 and Q.43, 2023 Q.8 and Q.20, 2024 Set 2 Q.37, 2025 Set 2 and 2026 Set 1 Q.10; Cayley-Hamilton has no verified CSE PYQ recorded at all, which is why that card is P3
